newsitem.title: USA: ITI Tech looks to new products, customers.
newsitem.headline: ITI Tech looks to new products, customers.

text.p: ITI Technologies Inc said Friday it hopes to announce some new customers in the next few weeks, while also relying on new security systems, to make up for the loss of orders from its largest customer.

"Hopefully in the next few weeks we'll be able to annouce some (customer) relationships," Jack Reichert, vice president of finance and administration for the North St. Paul, Minnesota, security system maker, said in an interview.
Earlier Friday, ITI said ADT Seucirty Systems Inc had told the company that ITI was currently not in ADT's "future strategic product planning."
"No one individual (customer) could replace them but two or three together could," Reichert said. ADT accounted for more than 43 percent of ITI's revenues through the third quarter of 1996, ITI said.
"We'll step back and retrench of course," Reichert said. "But we have a lot of new products and opportunities and developing relationships with new customers."
Among the new products is a newly released high-end security system and a lower-end wireless system to be released in 1997, Reichert said.
The company also has no debt and a "strong cash position" to help weather the ADT loss, Reichert said.
Reichert said ITI will "have to sit back and analyze" the decision by ADT, but it was not an expected move.

"We didn't really see this hapenning," he said. "To my knowledge, we didn't have any big issues with quality." He also said the there hadn't been any pricing move with ADT that he thought would have prompted ADT's decision.
Shares of ITI plunged 18-3/16 to 11-15/16 on Nasdaq Friday.
